Build strong stakeholder relationships and understand business priorities, operational impact and urgency. Coordinate onsite EUC support activities and assist with workload allocation to support timely completion of tasks. Act as a point of contact for technical escalations and business-critical incidents. Provide technical guidance, mentoring and knowledge sharing to team members. Support executive, VIP and business-critical operational users when required. Coordinate new starter, mover and leaver technology requirements. Collaborate with internal teams and stakeholders on project execution, incident resolution and service improvements. Service Management and ITIL Follow ITIL-aligned practices across Incident, Major Incident, Request, Problem and Change Management. Prioritise incidents according to business impact and urgency, including P1, P2, P3 and P4 classifications. Coordinate response and escalation for high-impact incidents and provide clear stakeholder updates. Monitor ageing tickets, SLA risks, backlog and escalations using ServiceNow or an equivalent ITSM platform. Ensure records contain appropriate troubleshooting notes, resolution details, categorisation and ownership. Identify recurring incidents and support Problem Management, root-cause analysis and post-incident reviews. Support on-call processes and after-hours escalation where required. Identify opportunities for automation, self-service and ticket deflection. Asset and Stock Management Manage hardware inventory, including laptops, desktops, mobile devices, peripherals and other EUC equipment. Maintain appropriate BAU, spare and replacement stock levels based on onboarding demand, refresh cycles, failures and project requirements. Maintain accurate asset records, stock sheets and asset management systems. Coordinate hardware receiving, inspection, asset tagging, secure storage, allocation and handover. Validate device enrolment and provisioning requirements, including Windows Autopilot, Microsoft Intune and Apple Business Manager where applicable. Coordinate device refresh, replacement, repair, warranty return, redeployment and disposal activities. Maintain chain of custody and support secure device sanitisation and disposal processes. Perform regular stock reconciliation, investigate discrepancies and produce inventory reports. Vendor and Stakeholder Coordination Coordinate with third-party vendors for equipment delivery, installation, maintenance, repair and replacement. Escalate and follow up vendor-supported issues involving devices such as kiosks, scanners, printers and specialised operational equipment. Maintain clear vendor support contacts, service expectations, warranty details and escalation pathways. Communicate technical issues, risks, progress and outcomes clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Project Delivery and BAU Transition Coordinate EUC workstreams for technology projects, deployments, refresh programs and site activities. Contribute to implementation plans, deployment schedules, pilot activities and phased rollouts. Identify operational risks, dependencies and support requirements before deployment. Coordinate onsite resources and vendors during implementation activities. Ensure appropriate testing and technical validation before production deployment. Confirm BAU ownership, support documentation, training, support model, spare stock and vendor escalation processes before project closure. Participate in post-implementation reviews and capture lessons learned. Security and Compliance Ensure endpoints comply with organisational security policies, configuration standards and approved software requirements. Support Microsoft Intune device compliance, endpoint enrolment and remediation of non-compliant devices. Support device encryption, endpoint protection, multifactor authentication and identity-related troubleshooting. Follow established processes for privileged access, data protection, software installation and secure handling of corporate equipment. Escalate suspected security incidents through established Cyber Security processes. Support secure user and device onboarding and offboarding activities. Knowledge and Continuous Improvement Create and maintain knowledge base articles, standard operating procedures, troubleshooting guides, checklists and operational runbooks. Document known errors, workarounds and recurring technical issues. Keep documentation current following technology, vendor or process changes. Identify and implement practical improvements that enhance user experience, service quality and operational efficiency. Share knowledge across Service Desk, Onsite Support and relevant technology teams. Desktop and Application Support Troubleshoot Outlook issues, including Non-Delivery Reports, message-header analysis, delegate permissions, deleted-item recovery, rules and Free/Busy issues. Support Microsoft

You'll lead delivery of funded projects and fee-for-service work, coordinate our casual facilitators, improve our systems and reporting, and get in the room with students and educators. Start date: Immediately Salary: Competitive NFP salary About Young Change Agents Young Change Agents (YCA) is a national not-for-profit social enterprise that equips young people aged 10–25 with the entrepreneurial mindset, skill set and toolset to create their own futures. Over the past 10 years, we have grown from a grassroots idea into a leading force in purpose-driven entrepreneurial education, reaching over 220,000 young people across Australia and internationally. With a strong foundation (1,900 schools across Australia and 4,400 educators), a co-designed program suite, a talented team and a national reputation, we are now poised to scale our reach to 2 million young people by 2030 and beyond. We believe entrepreneurial skills are one of the best ways to teach agency (the ability to shape the future) in a world that’s changing faster than the system can keep up. The role The Delivery Manager is responsible for planning, managing and reporting on all aspects of our projects. They make sure the experience for students, educators, facilitators and supporters upholds the promise, obligations and opportunities of our work. Working with a small yet mighty team, under direction from the CEO, this role leads and coordinates delivery within approved programs, budgets, funding agreements and YCA’s strategy. It balances facilitating workshops across the country, coordinating and supporting a strong team of facilitators, and managing the delivery of our pipeline of programs. What you’ll actually do Manage projects: Lead the end-to-end planning and execution of projects (grants, fee-for-service and pilots) within approved plans and funding agreements. Monitor timelines and deliverables, contribute to budget planning and tracking, and flag strategic opportunities with the teams. Accountability: Deliver what we promised, on time, on budget and in line with each program agreement. Escalate decisions about scope, budget or commitments to the CEO and executive team. Supervise and coordinate our casual facilitators and delivery resourcing, including recruitment, onboarding, rostering and development. Process and reporting: Our systems enable our scale. Update, automate and improve our project workflow, CRM, budgeting and reporting. Proactively look for insights that strengthen data integrity and continuous improvement. Represent and present: Facilitate in-person and online workshops and meetings with primary and high school students, educators and more. Role-model an entrepreneurial mindset, agency and what great delivery looks like. Build and follow through on relationships with diverse stakeholders, working towards our long-term vision Who we’re looking for Delivery: You have experience delivering programs or running operations in education, not-for-profit or community impact settings, ideally including different learning styles, design thinking and entrepreneurial learning. You care about giving young people the opportunity to develop and grow. (Formal teaching experience not required). Clever and calm coordination: You have a proven track record in multi-stakeholder projects where you were responsible for delivering results within defined timelines, budgets and agreements. You’re highly organised, accountable and process-oriented to deliver within complex, multi-stakeholder settings. Self-direction: You’re comfortable working remotely with a dispersed team. You’re a self-starter and culture creator who moves easily between in-person delivery, travel, meetings and online work.  Disposition: You think in systems and care about people. You can hold a project timeline and a relationship at the same time. A strong team player that is consistent without being rigid, and you’re honest about what’s working and what isn’t. Commerciality : Experience with fee-for-service and grant-funded delivery Practicalities include an Australian driver’s licence, a registered vehicle, a Working with Children Check or Blue Card, and the ability and willingness to travel . Toolset : Our team works in Slack, Google Workspace, Salesforce, Confluence, Canva, Jotform and Trello. Why join us? Join Young Change Agents as we scale our impact. You’ll be part of an ambitious, growing national organisation with a decade of experience and a team that’s smart, kind and deeply committed to young people. Together, we create opportunities for young people through entrepreneurship, community building and social enterprise, in a culture of creativity, collaboration and continuous improvement. Our work spans technology, inclusion, sustainability, health, space and design. The team you’d join We come from different backgrounds, but we share a few things. We are always asking, “How can we make this happen?” We are accountable to one another and have each other’s backs. We communicate honestly and with kindness. We look after our own health and wellbeing, and we speak up when we need to take time out. We love social enterprise as a model for creating social impact. Community and sustainability are at the heart of what we do. We are passionate about working with young people. As facilitators and mentors, we are present, patient and playful, and we quickly build rapport and mutual respect with youth. We are experienced in design thinking and lean startup, and we use them internally as well as externally. We love nothing more than helping teams think critically and creatively, and communicate their ideas well. This is a source of energy and motivation! We all share in Young Change Agents’ mission as a champion for teachers and youth workers. We value lifelong learning and building capacity in local communities to deliver quality education. We always encourage each other to grow and develop. We are multi-taskers. We like facilitating youth programs one day and liaising with corporate and government partners the next. We co-design and validate with our community and take feedback on board. We keep on top of reporting requirements and care about details. We are brand ambassadors for Young Change Agents, happy to represent YCA in business development, at networking events and as a speaker from time to time.. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you. How to Apply Email your application to hello@youngchangeagents.com by 9am AEDT Monday 23rd November 2026. Include a CV of no more than 2 pages and a cover letter of no more than 1 page outlining your experience in the key points of the role and why you’d like to join Young Change Agents.
